title: Choose the new utility direction
question: All three options move fcullmann.com toward the clear, light tool-platform style in your reference. Choose the balance of familiarity and personal identity.

options.label: Calm Tool Library
options.lineage: modern productivity libraries and desktop utility suites
options.thesis: A calm, spacious tool library where Florian introduces the collection in one concise band and the utilities become the main event.
options.viewport: A slim navigation bar, compact centered introduction, category filters, then a four-column tool grid with Featured tools first and writing visible at the fold.
options.risk: Its restraint depends on excellent spacing and icon craft; weak execution would feel merely generic.

raised.raise: Each category receives a confident color family instead of one timid accent scattered everywhere.
Tool names and categories remain exceptionally scannable at catalogue density.

options.label: Focused Utility Hub
options.lineage: best-in-class browser utility platforms with a personal product layer
options.thesis: A direct utility homepage with stronger product energy, a compact personal signature, and a grid designed to scale beyond fifty tools.
options.viewport: A restrained header, left-aligned professional introduction paired with a search-and-category control, then a dense five-column Featured tools shelf followed by the full catalogue.
options.risk: This is the most familiar solution and needs Florian’s voice and exact content hierarchy to avoid resembling another anonymous tool site.

options.label: Metro Tool Panorama
options.thesis: Tools become bold color tiles in a horizontally moving panorama.
options.viewport: Large colored tool tiles begin immediately beneath a minimal wordmark.
options.case: Excellent recognition but weaker professional context and long-catalogue scanability than the light utility directions.
options.risk: Too entertainment-led for a professional utility collection.

options.label: Teletext Tool Index
options.thesis: Every tool receives a direct numeric address in an extremely dense screen index.
options.viewport: A numbered tool directory fills the screen with keyboard-direct navigation.
options.case: Strong catalogue mechanics but conflicts with the light, contemporary reference and makes personal trust harder to establish.
options.kept: Exceptional scanability and explicit state labels.
options.risk: Retro character would dominate the actual tools.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.thesis: Pointer movement reveals tools as luminous wakes in a dark field.
options.viewport: A search gesture draws an illuminated path toward matching tools.
options.case: Memorable interaction, but search clarity, daylight usability, and the user’s light-platform preference all lose.
options.kept: Search feedback should feel immediate and alive.
options.risk: The effect would become the product instead of serving it.

canonCard.label: Straight Utility Catalogue
canonCard.thesis: The familiar browser-tool catalogue from the reference, executed cleanly and without an additional visual thesis.
canonCard.viewport: A compact header, centered title and description, category pills, then a six-column matrix of tools.
canonCard.risk: Immediately understandable but intentionally difficult to distinguish from established utility competitors.
